specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** workshop-agenda-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the logic of the workshop agenda by placing seven sessions in the correct order and naming what each session depends on, with at least 6 of 7 sessions in the correct position on the first commit. **Prerequisites:** Teacher Training Workshop, Workshop Agenda, and the calibration and improvement chapters (Chapters 14 and 15). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner arranges the seven sessions and commits the order once. A session is correct when it is in its position in the Content table. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 sessions in the correct position on the first commit. Rearranging before the commit is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The order of sessions is a matter of taste. (2) Improving a resource can come before checking the agent. (3) Peer review can come before the improvement. **Instructional Rationale:** Ordering sessions by what each one needs is an Apply-level action that tests why the sequence works. Each session depends on a product of an earlier one, so a wrong order shows a missing prerequisite. **Content:** The seven sessions in their correct order: | Position | Session | Depends on (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---| | 1 | Check-in and setup | Nothing, and it gives every teacher a working agent session. | | 2 | Why quality and reusability matter: the 10 metrics | The agent session is ready, and the metrics are needed to score. | | 3 | Calibration | The metrics, to score a sample by hand and with the agent. | | 4 | Checking the agent | The hand and agent scores from calibration. | | 5 | Improvement challenge | A verified evaluation, so the agent's output can be trusted. | | 6 | Peer review and publishing | A finished component to swap and re-score. | | 7 | Next steps: certificate requirements and the exit survey | Everything that came before. | **Provenance:** The order follows the sample one-day schedule in the book's workshop section. The sim leaves out the breaks and lunch, and says so. **Rules:** The sim presents the seven sessions in a shuffled order. Each position has exactly one correct session. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the seven sessions in a scrambled order. 2. The learner drags the sessions into the order they think is right, and may rearrange them freely. 3. The learner presses Commit. 4. The sim marks each session correct or misplaced, and shows what each misplaced session depends on. **Feedback:** One commit counts as evidence. The sim shows "[n] of 7 sessions in the correct position". At 6 or more it adds "You can plan a workshop day." Below 6 it lists the correct order with the dependency of each misplaced session. **Starting State:** The seven sessions in a shuffled order and the Commit button. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's agenda table and its explanation of why the order matters are the basis of this sim.
